title: Painted miniature of the Drowned Market

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone! I just finished painting my latest miniature from the Drowned Market expansion, and I’m honestly pretty proud of how it turned out. The detail on these figures is wild, especially with the weathered clothes and all those tiny trinkets hanging from their belts. I really tried to capture that murky, salty vibe the setting has—lots of blues and greens with a bit of rust on the weapons to show the wear from all the sea salt. It was a fun challenge to bring this particular character to life, especially since the lore makes them sound so mysterious and layered.

Also, I’ve been working on a bit of fan fiction to go along with the mini—trying to weave in some of the voice-acting nuances we’ve heard in the game-2 trailers. I’ve been imagining what conversations might sound like in those crowded, murky alleys where the market stands. There’s something about the way certain lines are delivered that really adds personality, and I wanted to capture that mood in the story. If anyone’s interested, I’d be happy to share some of the dialogue snippets or even a short audio clip I recorded myself!

Anyway, I’d love to hear what you all think, and if you’ve been working on anything similar or have tips for painting that rusty, wet look on minis. It feels like stepping into the drowned city itself when you get the colors right, and I’m always looking for new ideas. Can’t wait to see everyone’s creations from this awesome setting!

posts.cooked:
Wow, that painted miniature of the Drowned Market looks incredible! The way you captured the weathered wood and those waterlogged stalls really brings the scene to life. I especially love the tiny details like the hanging lanterns and the crates stacked precariously—those little touches make it feel like something right out of the game.

Also, the color choices really emphasize that moody, misty atmosphere of the market at dawn. It’s fun imagining all the whispered deals and secret exchanges happening in the mist. Have you thought about adding any little figures or maybe some water effects for extra realism? I bet a bit of gloss varnish on the puddles would make those docks shine even more!

By the way, I’m curious—did you base any of the poses or expressions on the voice-acting clips from the game? It would be amazing if you tried to capture some of the characters’ personalities through posture and detailing. Either way, this is an awesome piece, thanks for sharing!

posts.cooked:
Wow, this painted miniature of the Drowned Market looks incredible! The way you captured the weathered wood and the damp, mossy textures really brings the scene to life. It’s like you can almost hear the distant calls of merchants and the splash of waves against the dock. I love how you added those tiny details, like the crates piled precariously and the fishnet tangled on the post—makes the whole thing feel lived-in and authentic.

I’m also curious—did you take inspiration from any particular part of the game’s lore or the scripts from the voice-acting scenes? The market always struck me as a hub of whispers and secrets, so seeing it visualized like this sparks all kinds of ideas for stories and side quests. It would be awesome if someone could do a little fan-fiction based around a shady deal or a chase through those narrow walkways you’ve recreated here.

Thanks for sharing this! It’s cool to see fan art that goes beyond just characters and really fleshes out the world itself. Makes me want to dive back into game-2 and explore every corner. Keep us posted if you work on any other locations or maybe even some figures to go along with this!

posts.cooked:
Wow, that painted miniature of the Drowned Market looks incredible! You really captured the eerie, drowned vibe that the game nails so well in its underwater sections. The way you shaded the greenish hues on the wooden stalls and added those tiny barnacle details on the barrels gives it such an authentic feel. I especially love how you painted the little glimmers of bioluminescent coral scattered around the edges — it makes it look like it’s glowing softly in the deep, just like the game scenes with the ambient voice-acting really drive home.

Did you use any special techniques for those transparent water effects around the base? It looks like the market is actually submerged in murky water, and that adds so much atmosphere. Honestly, seeing this miniature makes me want to munch some kelp snacks while replaying the quests set in the Market’s back alleys, where all those shady characters have their whispered conversations with that haunting echo effect. It’s cool how this piece brings so much of Game-2’s vibe into a tangible form; have you thought about doing a little stop-motion or voice-over skit with it? I think fans would eat that up!

posts.cooked:
Wow, this is seriously impressive! The way you captured the murky, soaked vibe of the Drowned Market really brings the whole setting to life. I love how the layers of paint give that weathered, salt-stained feel to the miniatures—it’s like you can almost smell the briny air and hear the creaking of the old docks. The subtle shading on the tents and crates adds such depth, making each piece pop without feeling overdone.

Also, I remember you mentioned in a past post that you’re working on a little fanfic set in this part of the world, and I can totally see how this miniature influences your storytelling. It’s like the perfect physical anchor for the scenes with those shadowy traders and lost sailors. Plus, hearing your voice-acting clips tied to these characters earlier really helped me imagine how they’d sound in-game. Your dedication to making this world immersive across different mediums is super inspiring! Can’t wait to see what you come up with next.
